Marissa / Samir - thanks for the context. High-level answers and attachments below; happy to go deeper on the scheduled call.

1) Accepting customer-signed JWTs / service-account flow:
- Redwood supports validating JWTs signed by customer-managed service account keys. Validation uses the public key material you expose via standard jwks endpoints or via a provided public key. We do not require you to upload private keys.
- For Hosted customers, we validate tokens at the edge and maintain a lightweight JWKS cache with configurable TTL (default 5m). For Dedicated/Private customers, validation happens inside your VPC and you can configure cache TTL and refresh behavior.

2) Rotation & zero-downtime strategy:
- Recommended pattern: short-lived JWTs (1h) minted by your internal token service which uses a long-lived service account to sign. Rotate the signing key in KMS while continuing to expose the old public key in jwks until all tokens signed with it expire.
- Redwood's flow: on key rotation we support immediate revocation list updates and can be configured to accept a small grace window (configurable) to avoid blocking in-flight requests.
- See attached examples (sdk_jwt_rotation_examples.zip) which include a sample GCP KMS rotation script and a token-minting service pattern.

3) Scoping & least-privilege:
- You can map a single customer-per-environment to one service account (recommended) and create multiple scoped API keys for specific services (inference, embeddings, reranker) if you want fine-grained throttling/auditing.
- For Hosted, Redwood issues API keys scoped to route/model and environment. For Dedicated/Private, we recommend using your service accounts + JWT validation for full control.

4) Audit logs & retention:
- Hosted: token-level metrics and short-term request logs (90 days) are available.
- Dedicated: configurable retention up to 13 months (with add-on).
- Private (on-prem/VPC): retention controlled by customer's log aggregator; Redwood can emit structured auth events to your SIEM (syslog/Cloud PubSub).

Attachments included:
- redwood_authn_key_mgmt_playbook.pdf (playbook + recommended patterns)
- sdk_jwt_rotation_examples.zip (sample rotation scripts + SDK snippets)

Quick sample (from SDK snippets):

// Node example - validate incoming customer JWT (pseudo)
const jwks = await fetchJWKS('https://keys.fintechco.com/.well-known/jwks.json');
const payload = verifyJwt(token, jwks);
if (!payload.scope || !payload.env) throw new Error('invalid scope');
